morphology.shape: Spherical enveloped virion with a characteristic cone-shaped (conical) capsid core
morphology.notes: Reverse transcriptase converts the ssRNA genome into DNA, which integrates into the host cell genome — the defining feature of a retrovirus

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human CD4+ T lymphocytes and other CD4-receptor-bearing cells, including macrophages and dendritic cells
habitat.hostAssociation: Human pathogen, believed to have originated from zoonotic transmission of related simian immunodeficiency viruses
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Fragile outside the host; does not survive well on surfaces
habitat.reservoir: Chronically infected humans; a latent reservoir in resting CD4+ T cells complicates cure efforts

microscopy.appearance: Electron microscopy in research settings shows a spherical enveloped virion with a dense, cone-shaped internal capsid

culture.media: Not routinely cultured in clinical labs; specialized cell culture is used in research
culture.growthCharacteristics: Requires living CD4+ host cells; not grown on standard media

identificationClues: Diagnosed by antibody/antigen combination immunoassays and confirmatory testing, plus HIV RNA viral load — not by culture
Reverse transcriptase converts the ssRNA genome to DNA that integrates into the host genome
Cone-shaped (conical) capsid is distinctive among retroviruses
Preferentially infects and progressively depletes CD4+ T lymphocytes

diseases: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) — advanced, untreated disease with severe CD4+ depletion and opportunistic infections
virulenceFactors: Reverse transcriptase — enables genome integration and a high mutation rate that aids immune evasion
gp120/gp41 envelope glycoproteins — CD4 and co-receptor binding for cell entry
High replication and mutation rate — rapid immune escape and drug resistance
clinicalImportance.transmission: Blood and body fluids — sexual contact, blood exposure such as shared needles or transfusion, and perinatal (mother-to-child) transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A major global public health issue; antiretroviral therapy has transformed HIV infection into a manageable chronic condition where treatment is accessible, though significant global disparities in access remain
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Combination antigen/antibody immunoassays are used for initial screening, with supplemental/confirmatory testing and viral load quantification guiding diagnosis and management

examFacts.shape: Enveloped virion with a conical capsid core
examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not applicable — diagnosed by immunoassay and viral load, not biochemical tests
examFacts.importantDisease: HIV infection, progressing to AIDS if untreated
examFacts.importantTest: Fourth-generation antigen/antibody immunoassay; HIV RNA viral load
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Conical capsid core and reverse-transcriptase-mediated genome integration, characteristic of retroviruses
